issue.title: Agents-sidecar hoods have no retention: owner manifests, hood snapshots, and index-render cost grow without bound
issue.description:
The v2 agents sidecar has no retention story: every hood ever published by an owner
machine stays in that owner's `manifest.json` and on disk forever. On athena's sase
manifest (`users/bbugyi200/machines/athena/manifest.json` in the `sase--agents`
sidecar) this reached 2043 hoods / 71,899 recorded file paths / 4.19 MB in ~4 months of
use, which is what let the manifest hit the 4 MiB read cap and brick publication
(bead sase-10x, fixed by slimming the manifest format and raising caps).

That fix raises the ceiling (slim entries, ~16k-hood decode cap) but does not remove
the unbounded growth: hood count, snapshot files, published run pages, and the
O(total-hoods) per-publish work (reading every snapshot and re-rendering index pages in
`load_validated_publication` / `render_browsing_payload`) all still grow monotonically.
At current creation rates (~2000 hoods/month on one machine) the new caps are roughly a
year of headroom, and per-publish latency degrades continuously before that.

Discovered while diagnosing sase-10x / the sase-11l.2 page 404 on 2026-09-16; filed
separately because retention is a different remediation with real design questions the
byte-cap fix deliberately avoided:

- Which hoods are prunable (age of newest run? beyond newest-K? closed-epic hoods?),
  and what "pruned" means: drop the manifest entry only (pages stay as unvalidated,
  unindexed history) vs. move pages to an archive area vs. delete them.
- Page-permalink stability: bead pages, commit messages, and notes link to
  `agents/<global>/README.md` and `families/<global>.md` permalinks; pruning must not
  break those (or must consciously accept it).
- Cross-machine semantics: manifests are owner-sharded, so retention can run
  per-owner, but shared index pages must render consistently while owners disagree
  about retention state.
- Interaction with `sase agent sync --repair-manifest`, which currently re-adopts any
  on-disk hood the manifest omits and would resurrect pruned hoods unless taught
  otherwise.

Note: the in-progress sase-zw disk-retention epic chain covers local host disk
footprint, not this published-sidecar corpus; the two are related in philosophy only.

task_type_fields.impact: Publication latency degrades continuously with corpus size (215 drain-timeout failures already recorded in the gh_sase-org__sase publication outbox), and the slim-manifest caps introduced to fix sase-10x are only ~a year of headroom before publication bricks again.
task_type_fields.location: agents sidecar owner manifests and hood corpus (src/sase/agents_sync/publication_planning.py, publication_validation.py, v2_manifest_io.py); athena example users/bbugyi200/machines/athena/manifest.json
task_type_fields.repro: On athena: python3 -c "import json; m=json.load(open('/home/bryan/.sase/projects/gh_sase-org__sase/repos/agents/users/bbugyi200/machines/athena/manifest.json')); print(len(m['hoods']))" shows 2000+ hoods after ~4 months, growing ~2000/month with no mechanism that ever removes one; every publish re-reads all hood snapshots and re-renders index pages over the full set.
